newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - LONDON EVENING STANDARD - APRIL 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Carlton Television's Michael Green was today the latest victim of a gang of robbers who have been targeting the rich in London. Mr Green was ambushed along with his wife as they arrived at their Mayfair home.

Professor Tim Congdon, director of Lombard Street Research has warned that a Labour Chancellor is likely to raise revenue by hitting tax relief on pension funds. He says abolition of 20 percent advance corporation tax and associated ACT tax credits payable to those investors exempt from tax would raise six billion stg.
DAEWOO SECURITIES' FIRST LOSS IN 17 YEARS
South Korea's biggest broking house Daewoo Securities has made its first loss in 17 years, proving that powerful companies are not immune to economic difficulties.
COURT TO RULE ON CHEAP CIGARETTES

The European Court of Justice was set to make a ruling today on whether companies can act as agents to import duty-paid cigarettes. The move would revolutionise the British tobacco retailing industry whilst the government would lose millions of pounds in excise duties.
BUMPER PROFITS BUT A CLOUD OVER WALL STREET

Big securities firms on Wall Street are presenting a boom in profits for the first three months of 1997, however the market downturn in March is now exacting a heavy toll. The firms hit new highs in investment banking fees but ever before the Federal Reserve announced an interest rate increase on March 11 future deals looked scarce.
